content: 1. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is advised, and caution should be exercised. 2. Ethinyl estradiol may enhance the effects of naratriptan through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 3. Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 4. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended, and close monitoring is necessary. 5. Nemolizumab decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by increasing CYP enzyme activity, likely due to cytokine suppression. This may lead to reduced systemic levels of sensitive CYP substrates. Dosage adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 6. Neomycin (oral) decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. 8. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of nicardipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 9. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 10. Nirmatrelvir decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by increasing its metabolism, possibly through ritonavir-mediated CYP2C9 or CYP1A2 induction. Additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended for the remainder of the cycle, and close monitoring is necessary. 11. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by increasing its metabolism. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended for the remainder of the cycle, and close monitoring is required. 12. Nitrofurantoin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Ethinyl estradiol may increase the levels of nortriptyline by an unspecified mechanism, potentially decreasing oxidative metabolism of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs). This may lead to increased serum concentrations of antidepressants and a higher risk of TCA-related adverse effects. Close monitoring is recommended. 14. Ofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of olanzapine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 16. Omaveloxolone decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing weak CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. 17. Ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir with or without dasabuvir is contraindicated with ethinyl estradiol due to an unspecified interaction mechanism. Co-administration has been associated with significant ALT elevations in clinical trials. Ethinyl estradiol-containing medications should be discontinued before initiating this hepatitis C regimen and restarted approximately two weeks after completion. 18. Otesecazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting BCRP. This may increase the risk of toxicities of BCRP substrates. Dosage adjustments of BCRP substrates may be required, and close monitoring is advised. 19. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. 20. Paromomycin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 21. Penicillin G aqueous decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by increasing its metabolism. There is a risk of oral contraceptive failure. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 22. Penicillin VK decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. 24. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. 25. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. 26. Pioglitazone decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol through an unknown mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 27. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 28. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. 29. Ethinyl estradiol may increase the levels of protriptyline by an unspecified mechanism, potentially decreasing oxidative metabolism of TCAs. This may lead to increased serum concentrations of antidepressants and a higher risk of TCA-related adverse effects. Close monitoring is recommended. 30. Quinidine increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. 31. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 32. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of ramelteon by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 33. Ranolazine increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. 34. Rasagiline levels may be increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP1A2 inhibition. Caution and close monitoring are recommended, especially with CYP1A2 inhibitors. 35. Repotrectinib decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. 36. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. 39. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. 40. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended, and close monitoring is necessary. 41. Romidepsin decreases the effects of ethinyl estradiol through receptor binding competition. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 42. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of ropinirole by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 43. Rosuvastatin increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 44. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dosage adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be required, and close monitoring is advised. 45. Rufinamide decreases the effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing weak CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and close monitoring is recommended. 46. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 47. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib topical by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 48. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels of selegiline by inhibiting N-demethylation. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 49. Siltuximab may restore CYP450 enzymatic activity by inhibiting IL-6, which is downregulated by infection and inflammation. Caution is advised when co-administered with CYP substrates that have a narrow therapeutic index. 50. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the levels or effects of somapacitan by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Higher doses of growth hormone analogs may be required, and close monitoring is recommended. 51. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the levels or effects of somatrogon by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Higher doses of growth hormone analogs may be required, and close monitoring is recommended. 52. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the levels or effects of somatropin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Higher doses of growth hormone analogs may be required, and close monitoring is recommended. 53. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. 54. Stiripentol affects the metabolism of ethinyl estradiol by acting as both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer. Dosage adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be required, and close monitoring is recommended. 55. Sugammadex decreases the effects of ethinyl estradiol by receptor binding competition. A sugammadex bolus dose is equivalent to missing doses of hormonal contraceptives. Additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended for the next seven days.
